description: A six-panel composite TEM figure on a TD (transverse-direction) sample of a low-density medium-Mn steel deformed to 15% engineering strain, arranged as two rows. Row (a): (a1) is a bright-field (BF) micrograph with a 500 nm scale bar showing two dark bands of strain-induced α'-martensite (red arrow) growing between regions labelled γ (austenite, left) and α (ferrite, right); (a2) is the corresponding dark-field (DF) image in which the same α'-martensite bands appear bright. Row (b): (b1) BF image with a 500 nm scale bar where α'-martensite is arrowed at two separate sites adjacent to a γ grain, with a δ (delta-ferrite) region labelled at the bottom; (b2) is the matching DF image highlighting the α'-martensite in bright contrast. To the right of both rows sit two indexed selected-area diffraction patterns: an FCC pattern, zone axis Z = [011], with reflections labelled (-200), (-11-1) and (-1-11), and a BCC pattern, zone axis Z = [-111], with reflections labelled (01-1), (110) and (101). The phase-contrast in BF/DF combined with the FCC/BCC diffraction identifies the α'-martensite and the surrounding γ/α/δ phases, and the figure demonstrates that α'-martensite nucleates at or close to γ/α and γ/δ phase boundaries. No numeric strain or crystallographic values are printed on the panels beyond the scale bars and index labels.

observations.observation: The group is a composite TEM figure with two rows, each row pairing a BF and a DF micrograph with two indexed SAED patterns shown on the right.
Panels (a1) and (b1) are bright-field images and (a2) and (b2) are dark-field images; the α'-martensite is dark in BF and bright in DF at the same locations.
All four micrographs carry a 500 nm scale bar in the lower-left corner.
The diffraction patterns are indexed as FCC with zone axis Z = [011] (reflections (-200), (-11-1), (-1-11)) and BCC with zone axis Z = [-111] (reflections (01-1), (110), (101)).
Panel (a1) shows dark α'-martensite bands (red arrow) located between a γ-labelled (austenite) region and an α-labelled (ferrite) region.
Panel (b1) shows α'-martensite arrowed at two locations adjacent to a γ grain, with a δ (delta-ferrite) region labelled at the bottom of the field.
The figure is TEM observation of austenite deformation mechanisms in the TD sample at engineering strain 15%.

The BF/DF image pairs and corresponding diffraction patterns were taken from two representative austenite grains and show strain-induced α'-martensite nucleation close to γ/α and γ/δ phase boundaries.
The results confirm that strain-induced α'-martensite is nucleated at or close to γ/α and γ/δ phase boundaries.
The nucleation is rationalized by high strain and stress concentrations at interface regions, resulting from strain incompatibility between adjacent phases, which enhance dislocation activity.
Defects such as ledges at interfaces are proposed as favorable sites for activation of multiple slip systems.
For some other austenite grains α'-martensite has not yet formed; those observations belong to Fig. 7, not this figure.
